first.rationale: Two symptoms (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) point at the funnel itself, and memory_86/memory_31 both say shortening onboarding and cutting signup fields lift completion and early adoption. That makes onboarding simplification the direction most likely to address the root cause rather than paper over it, so it is my intended action. Verification budget goes to the two beliefs that are simultaneously most consequential here and most weakly supported for the stated objective. memory_73 (promotional pricing) is the obvious reflex against a competitor's entry pricing, and it is recorded only as 'acquisition and revenue lift' — it says nothing about who those discounted accounts become. Price-led acquisition classically imports low-willingness-to-pay, high-churn cohorts, so a memory measured on top-line acquisition cannot license a decision optimized for sustainable qualified revenue; I want the original record to see whether retention or expansion was ever tracked past the promo window. memory_86 gets the second pull because it is the belief I am actually about to act on, and its endpoints (completion rate, time-to-value, 'early product adoption') are all proxies upstream of revenue. Faster completion can mean less qualification and thinner activation if the removed steps were doing real filtering work — the same mechanism that could explain part of the current activation dip if prior simplifications already shipped. I need to know the measurement horizon and whether downstream account quality held. I deliberately did not spend budget on memory_57 or memory_44: memory_57 already carries an explicit retention check, and memory_44 is scored on pipeline quality, which is close to the objective — both are better supported on the dimension I care about, and neither is the action I am taking this week. Scale is a small guarded test rather than broad rollout: inherited memories are 24–52 days old, the environment has visibly shifted with the competitor launch, and I should not treat archived proxy wins as settled under new conditions. Guardrails should track not just completion but downstream activation quality and 30/60-day retention of the simplified cohort, so a proxy win that degrades account value is visible before it is scaled. If the memory_73 record turns out to include durable retention evidence, promotional pricing becomes a live contender for the next slot; if memory_86 turns out to be short-horizon only, I hold the simplification narrow and instrument it harder rather than abandoning it.

final.rationale: Both pulls paid off, and in opposite directions. exp_73 confirms the failure mode I suspected: the 40% SMB discount bought +31% signup and +18% qualified revenue on a top-line read, but -12% 30-day retention — the cohort does not survive first renewal. The original record even carries an explicit do-not-generalize warning that had been stripped out during consolidation into memory_73. Under an objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, promotional pricing is not merely unproven, it is affirmatively disconfirmed, and it would have been exactly the wrong reflex against the competitor's entry pricing. Matching a price attack by importing a churning cohort trades durable revenue for a quarter of flattering acquisition numbers. exp_86 survives verification at the endpoint I actually cared about: completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days are proxies, but 30-day retention +3% means the shortening did not achieve completion by stripping out qualification. The proxy win and the value-relevant outcome move together, which is the specific thing I could not assume from the consolidated summary. So I commit the slot to simplify_onboarding. It is also the direction best matched to the actual diagnosis: onboarding completion -4% and activation -6% are funnel symptoms, and treating them at the funnel is root-cause work, whereas discounting would have papered over a retention problem with an acquisition number. memory_31 and memory_91 point the same way and are consistent with the verified record, though neither was independently checked. Scale moves from small guarded test to standard experiment because the belief I am acting on was verified on the dimension that matters, not because the environment got safer. I still flag downstream value risk: exp_86 ran on day-52 conditions, the competitor launch has changed the inbound mix, and a shortened flow interacts differently with price-shopping traffic than with the original cohort. Instrument beyond completion — track activation quality, 30- and 60-day retention, and expansion for the treated cohort, and hold the rollout if completion rises while retention flattens or falls, since that is the signature of the exp_73 failure appearing in a different wrapper. Two memory corrections should be written back: memory_73 must be amended to carry the -12% retention finding and the do-not-generalize conclusion so no future session reads it as a clean win, and memory_86 should be marked source-verified with its retention endpoint attached. memory_31, memory_57, memory_44 and memory_91 remain unverified and should keep that status rather than inheriting confidence from this round.
